text:
marta: Heads-up — starting compatibility bakeoff for Goldfinch LoRA merge (cust: Goldfinch). Dropping a tiny eval pack + smoke configs. Can ppl run int4 and fp16 pass and report token-likelihood and a few response diffs? link: https://redwood.internal/evals/goldfinch/quickpack :eyes:
kevin: Got it. Which base model did you graft onto? any tokenizer tweaks?
marta: Base is redwood/rw-13b-open, tokenizer unchanged. Merge used LoRA alpha=32, r=8. No vocab edits. Quick metrics from local fp16 smoke run (sampled 200 prompts): avg logprob delta ~ -0.02, top-k overlap 0.98, latency +12% on p3.2xlarge.
raj: Can you paste the quant config you want for int4? I'll run on the rack tonight.
marta: Sure — using our standard quant config but with per-channel fallback on MLPs. snippet:
```
--quant-mode int4
--quant-scheme q4_0
--per-channel-fallback layers:mlp
--kvcache true
--batch 4
```
kevin: Noted. For int4, watch numeric drift on currency/date tokens — Goldfinch has a lot of invoice examples. Add the invoice prompt set to the smoke pack.
sophie: Quick heads-up: in the fp16 diff there were 3/200 cases where the LoRA introduced minor hallucinations on 'payment timeline' questions (dates invented). I flagged them in the eval gist.
marta: @sophie can you drop the exact examples here? we'll add them to the fail-cases set. If it's concentrated on temporal reasoning we might need a targeted prompt-tune or a tiny dataset to anchor dates.
sophie: paste: 
1) "When was invoice #983 paid?" -> LoRA: "Paid on July 14th" (no payment date in context)
2) "Expected settlement for order 210" -> LoRA adds a 3-day estimate, base abstains
3) "Is invoice 0312 overdue?" -> LoRA: says "Overdue by 2 days" but source shows nothing
raj: That's helpful. I can run int4 with the invoice prompts as a separate eval and compare abstain rates and hallucination counts. I'll also run a deterministic seed to check stochasticity.
eval-bot: automated-eval summary: fp16: pass (top-k overlap>0.95), int4: warn (numeric drift observed, 12 flagged examples across 500 prompts). Full report: https://redwood.internal/evals/goldfinch/report/1736789012
kevin: If int4 drift is concentrated, maybe we can enable per-token scaling or keep MLPs in fp16 and quantize attention. Tradeoff latency vs correctness.
marta: Agreed. For customer demo next week we should present fp16 baseline and a guarded int4 config (mlp fp16, attn int4). Raj, can you run that hybrid config and upload logs?
raj: On it. Running hybrid now with this command:
```bash
redwood-eval run --model redwood/rw-13b-open --lora goldfinch-v1 --quant hybrid --mlp-fp16 true --eval-set goldfinch-smoke-invoice --seed 42 --out /tmp/gf-hybrid.json
```
marta: Thanks. Also adding a routing suggestion: for Goldfinch production we might pin high-risk routes (invoices, settlements) to fp16 until we get pass rate >99%. lower-risk chat can use int4.
kevin: Good plan. Add a note for the Console: per-route model overrides + metric gating on hallucination rate.
sophie: quick note — one more small behavioral diff: LoRA sometimes flips 'payer' vs 'payee' in ambig names. I'll enumerate examples.
marta: please drop them here. If it's only a few cases we can add a tiny fine-tune pass to fix label alignment.
raj: Hybrid run finished, initial numbers: latency ~ +6% vs int4, hallucination flags down to 3/500, top-k overlap 0.975. Uploading artifact to the eval report.
eval-bot: artifact uploaded: /artifacts/goldfinch/hybrid-run-1736789300.json
kevin: Thanks all. Next steps: raj to run hybrid full smoke with seed variants, marta to prepare demo slides showing fp16 vs hybrid tradeoffs, sophie to compile flagged examples into a repair set.
marta: acked. I'll ping sales with the tuned fallback plan. TY! :thumbsup:
